Independent School in Wokingham, Berkshire
Reddam House Berkshire
Exceptional Private Learning in Berkshire, UK
Reddam House Berkshire is a world-class co-educational day and boarding school in Berkshire, UK.
Considered ‘Outstanding and Excellent in every area’ by ISI in 2022, Reddam House welcomes students from all over the world to our exceptional facilities, set in 125 acres of parkland. Our classes are taught in a magnificent restored Victorian mansion which has been transformed into an extraordinary learning environment.
Our school in Wokingham, Berkshire has an internationally respected curriculum to ensure our students consistently achieve outstanding grades in GCSEs and A-levels, with over 90% securing places at top-tier universities in the UK and abroad.
From our youngest learners (3 months), to our Sixth Form students, our approach to the curriculum balances academic achievement alongside sports and the performing arts, to inspire and instil a love of learning in our students that will stay with them forever.
Why Choose Our Private School in Wokingham, Berkshire?
At our independent school in Wokingham, Berkshire, we provide students from all over the world with a superlative private education. Students benefit from our internationally respected curriculum, alongside a broad range of academic, cultural and sporting activities, and the most comprehensive programme of enrichment activities in the county.
In our secure, relaxed and self-disciplined environment, we nurture the individuality, talent and self-assurance of all our students. Alongside our world-class curriculum, this child-centric approach is what sets us apart from other schools in Wokingham.
Our unique Cycle Test programme offers valuable insights into each pupil's learning progress, while cutting-edge technology tools such as our Global Study Platform and Metaverse VR, help us to equip every student with the skills they need to achieve academic success. Our exclusive Challenge and Extension programme also provides students with an additional opportunity to expand their learning and skills.
At Reddam House we understand the importance of education and we prepare our students to face the future with pride and confidence - inspiring true excellence in international education.
World Class Academic Results
Our students achieve consistently outstanding grades in GCSE and A-Level, all above the national UK average.
Entrance to a Top-Tier University
90% of our students are offered a place at their 1st choice university globally
An All-Through School with Outstanding Facilities
An inspiring education with flexible boarding options & top facilities for academics, sports and the arts, from 3 months to 18 years.
An Extensive Enrichment Programme and Outstanding Pastoral Care
A curriculum taught by specialist teachers to nurture talent and achieve results
Early Learning School
3 months to 4+ years
Junior School
Middle School
Senior School
Outstanding Academic Results
At Reddam House we are known for our consistently high level of academic achievement.
Our A-level and GCSE results reflect this and are all significantly higher than the UK national average (more than double for grades 9-7 at GCSE), and better than most other schools in Berkshire.
These results are testament not just to our teaching, but our students' outstanding ambition, commitment, and spirit.
2026 A Level Exam Results
Congratulations to our students on their outstanding A-Levels. We are immensely proud of your achievements and excited for what comes next. Your stellar results reflect the world-class education and future-ready mindset we nurture from day one.
'Outstanding and Excellent in every area' according to the 2022 ISI Report
At Reddam House Berkshire we are proud to have been awarded ‘outstanding’ in the Early Learning Years Foundation Stage and ‘Excellent’ from Y1 to Y13 in our ISI-Focused Compliance and Educational Quality Inspection Report. Read the full report here and discover some of the report highlights below:
"Pupils' academic and other achievements are excellent. Many pupils participate in a wide range of extra-curricular activities linked to the school's aims for excellence in academics, sports and performing arts. Pupils enter a wide variety of competitions in which they achieve notable success: national poetry competitions, public speaking, computing, dance, art, mathematics and music competitions. Sports teams consistently achieve success in regional and local competitions with a large number of pupils selected to represent the county in a variety of sports."
"The overall effectiveness of the early years provision is outstanding."
"The curriculum is extremely well implemented in order to meet the unique needs of each child and is regularly monitored and evaluated by leaders to fully understand its impact on learning."
"There is an ethos of respect, support, kindness, and openness across the entire community, where pupils value their relationships with individuals and groups and make a positive contribution to the school and local community."
"Pupils show an excellent understanding of diversity in what is an extremely diverse school"
Awards and Accreditations
Muddy's Best Schools Award - Experiential Learning
Reddam House Berkshire is a member of the prestigious Inspired Education Group, made up of 121 premium schools and teaching over 95,000 students worldwide. Inspired Education sets a new standard in world-class private education, with exceptional teachers and an unparalleled commitment to excellence.
Inspired students benefit from extraordinary global exchange programmes and summer camps, as well as unique opportunities for collaboration and curriculum partnerships with the Inspired Schools' community.
Specialist University Counselling
Specialist University Counselling
All Inspired students receive university and career guidance from specialist local counsellors in each school. Students wishing to secure a place at leading universities in the UK and USA can also benefit from special rates with our university counselling partners: Arete Education and The Classroom Door.
Our carefully selected teachers are subject specialists who deliver engaging lessons at all school levels. The Inspired Group exclusively recruits highly qualified, talented educators with stellar reputations for all its schools, and we prioritise outstanding tuition and student safety.
Global Exchange Opportunities
Global Exchange Opportunities
Inspired's Global Exchange Programme gives pupils a unique opportunity to experience other Inspired schools around the world. Students benefit from collaborating with their global peers and the experience helps them to build valuable networks and lifelong friendships - enriching their social, linguistic and academic skills, expanding their horizons and perspectives.
International Group of Premium Schools
International Group of Premium Schools
In addition to being an Inspired School, Reddam House Berkshire is part of the Reddam House group, a community of premium schools in South Africa, Australia and the UK. Reddam House Schools offer a definitive statement of excellence in private education, where each school is committed to helping students discover the full extent of their potential.
Discover how choosing Reddam House Berkshire for your child's education can be the best investment in their successful future.

Book an exclusive tour of our inspiring campus to experience our school culture and environment first-hand.
As part of the tour, parents will have the chance to explore various parts of our magnificent school campus, including our advanced learning spaces and sports facilities. They will also meet with senior members of our academic and admissions teams to ask any questions they may have.
Tour Duration: 45 to 60 minutes
We have availability for personalised tours on most days. Please book a convenient appointment using the booking form below. We look forward to welcoming your family to Reddam House!

Scholarships
Inspiring Scholarship Opportunities at Reddam House Berkshire
To be a scholar at Reddam House is a major achievement and a source of pride for staff and parents alike. We grant scholarships across our three pillars: Academics, Sport and Performing Arts. We also offer the Nsouli scholarships, and the Inspired Scholarship Programme.
Our school awards scholarships to recognise unique abilities or achievements in the fields of Academics, Art, Sport and Performing Arts (Drama, Dance and Music). We only grant a small number of scholarships in each discipline, recognising excellence in a student’s chosen field. These scholarships are awarded at our key admissions entry points of Year 7, Year 9 and Year 12. Occasionally, we may consider offering a scholarship outside of these age groups to outstanding individuals.
We expect and support our scholars to take full advantage of the opportunities available at Reddam House, which can lay the foundations for success at the very best global universities and in their future careers.
For more information about our unique scholarships and the criteria and conditions for each one, please refer to the booklet below.
Scholarships Brochure
Applications for scholarships are open to all but can only be achieved by those who meet the entry requirements. To apply for a Reddam House scholarship, please register and complete the scholarship application form on our admissions portal.
Nsouli Scholars
A Transformative Opportunity
The Nsouli Scholars Programme is an exciting global initiative that promises to transform lives by enabling 50 extraordinary students at any one time to attend any of Inspired’s prestigious schools on a full scholarship for the duration of their education. The ambition is that the scholarship will provide hundreds of children with an opportunity to receive a truly transformative education.
By opening this path to exceptional individuals, we hope to expand our community, and to empower children of all backgrounds with unrivalled opportunities in academics, sports, the arts and extracurricular activities. In this sense, the Nsouli Scholars Programme is an investment both in education and in shaping the leaders of tomorrow.
This generous endowment honours Nadim Nsouli, who founded Inspired in 2013 as a definitive statement of excellence in private international education. In recognition of Mr Nsouli’s Lebanese heritage and Inspired’s commitment to inclusivity, several scholarships will be awarded to individuals of Lebanese origin.
Inspired Scholarship Programme
The Inspired Scholarship Programme has been created to make a premium education more accessible to families who believe in the power of learning to open up lives. Offering discounted tuition scholarships, the programme supports prospective students who aspire to make the most of an Inspired education.
Inspired schools offer a world-class educational experience that combines academics and engaging extra-curricular activities, producing confident, multi-skilled students who flourish in a competitive and increasingly interconnected world. Along with expert instruction by hand-picked teachers, our students access specialist sports programmes and professional tutelage from leaders in the performing and creative arts. As a result, they leave armed with a robust value system and a love of learning that extends well beyond the classroom.
Inspired is also committed to leveraging new and transformative learning technologies. Inspired AI empowers children to achieve academic excellence by delivering actionable insights that are unique to each student, including strengths and weaknesses. Our partnership with The Royal College of Music and Forte, a revolutionary online platform, enables children to receive personalised music tuition from professionals. Students with musical interests benefit from bespoke private lessons, advancing their practice as creatives and gaining valuable performance experience.
The advantages of our holistic approach to education are evidenced by the fact that Inspired students consistently excel in academic performance, surpassing national and global averages. In 2022, the Average Point Score was 35 for those undertaking the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, for which the world average was 31.98, while A* scores comprised 27% of our students' A Level grades, compared to 14.6% globally. As a consequence, many are able to attend leading universities, with one in three graduates going on to a Russell Group University or Ivy League College.
The Inspired Group includes top-rated day and boarding schools worldwide, meaning students enjoy access to a diverse international community. Be it through specialised Summer Camps or immersive Global Exchange Programmes, children have the chance to travel broadly and engage meaningfully with different cultures, meet and learn from our esteemed partners, build lifelong networks, and become more independent.
Still have questions about the scholarships available at our school? Our admissions team will be delighted to assist you.

University Destinations
Unlimited Possibilities for Your Life After Reddam House Berkshire
With an education from Reddam House Berkshire, your child will be ready to excel at university and their future career. The excellent preparation, consistently outstanding results in external examinations, and expert university counselling provided ensure that the majority of our graduates secure acceptance to their preferred university courses in the United Kingdom and abroad.
Over the years, our students have advanced to the most prestigious universities in the UK, from Oxford and Cambridge to other well-respected Russell Group institutions such as Warwick, Durham, King's, Imperial, Southampton, Manchester, Bristol, and Exeter. They have also excelled at other renowned institutions, including Royal Holloway, Loughborough, and Bath University.
In our globalized world, more and more Reddam House students are pursuing their higher education studies abroad, with continental Europe (namely, Germany, Italy, or the Netherlands), the United States or Japan as the most popular destinations.
View our Leavers' Destinations
Secure Your Child's Acceptance to a World-Leading University
Reddam House Berkshire is a proud member of Inspired Education, a global leading group of premium schools around the world. Despite fierce competition for admission to prestigious institutions, 1 in 3 Inspired graduates secure a place at Russell Group and Ivy League universities, with an impressive 9 out of 10 gaining acceptance to their first-choice universities.
As navigating the university application process nowadays can be daunting, with over a hundred universities in the UK alone, all senior students at Reddam House receive dedicated support from a team of expert university counsellors, well-versed in the admissions procedures of top universities in the UK and abroad. These counsellors also possess a deep understanding of national universities' unique entry criteria and course suitability, enabling every student to plan their future path long before graduation.
Exclusive Partnerships to Help You Achieve Your Goals
In light of the increasing number of applicants in recent years, top UK and US universities have become exceptionally competitive to enter. To ensure students have the best chance of success, Inspired has introduced carefully chosen partnerships for expert guidance in securing a coveted place at their desired world-class institutions: Arete Education and The Classroom Door are global leaders in UK and US university admissions counselling and offer Inspired students preferential rates.
Ignite the Future with Arete Educational Consulting
Arete Educational Consulting is a full-service tutoring and educational consulting company dedicated to helping students of all ages achieve their academic dreams and aspirations. Their services range from boosting students' standardised test scores to personalised tutoring sessions or guiding them through the entire university application process, facilitating their admission to top-tier universities. This invaluable support fosters a lasting connection with effective learning routines that students can apply to their future academic endeavours.
Securing a place at a prestigious US or UK university is a formidable task. Inspired's collaboration with Arete streamlines the admissions process, offering customised learning packages tailored to each student's needs. Students who choose Arete are paired with dedicated counsellors several years prior to applying to university. Counsellors provide guidance on summer working experiences, extracurricular involvement, and university requirements. With proper preparation, students can embark on the application process with a competitive edge.
Arete's coaches are committed to inspiring academic excellence and bolstering student confidence. They identify and overcome potential obstacles. Alongside university counselling, Arete excels in providing tuition in languages, mathematics, sciences, humanities, and study skills. They also offer one-on-one coaching for school entrance and college admission exams, including the SAT.
When enquiring, please mention that you are an Inspired student to access special rates.
Visit Arete's Website
The Classroom Door
Inspired understands that enhancing a student's prospects of securing admission at a US or UK university can be a costly endeavour. That is why we have joined forces with The Classroom Door (TCD), a comprehensive educational platform and tutoring marketplace. TCD strives to be more budget-friendly than many other counselling and tutoring programmes while adhering to a social mission of providing accessibility to elite tutoring and the college application process. You can receive tutoring from expert advisors, Ivy League-educated tutors, or certified teachers starting at just $15 per hour. Proper preparation equips students with the best possible start to their application process in a highly competitive environment.
TCD boasts an impressive pool of 1,500 world-class tutors and counsellors hailing from renowned institutions such as Harvard, Yale, MIT, Stanford, Princeton, and Oxford. These professionals offer expert counselling to guide students through the application process, with a strong track record of successful university placements. TCD also offers access to exclusive college counselling content developed by its founder, Nikki Geula, an industry pioneer in college consulting and tutoring. The subscription-based self-guided college counselling lessons cover all aspects of college admissions, including essay drafting, building a college list, and insights and tips for Ivy League applications.
One-on-one tutoring spans from kindergarten enrichment to standardised test preparation, including SAT, ACT, GRE, GMAT, MCAT, ESL, and various language courses for all proficiency levels. To access our preferential rates, simply type the code 'INSPIRED10' on The Classroom Door app when booking
Visit the Classroom Door Website

These links are included for information and convenience and Inspired has no control of the content of the website nor services offered by Arete Educational Consulting and The Classroom Door. Therefore, Inspired accepts no responsibility for the content or any services provided by them. For further information, please see Website Terms and Conditions.

Nursery School in Wokingham, Berkshire
Nursery Education at Reddam House Berkshire
3 months to 4+ years, Early Learning School
Our private Nursery School in Wokingham, Berkshire, is where our exceptional early education thrives in each of our dedicated classrooms and outstanding outdoor facilities.
Children from 3 months to 4 years learn based on a 'rhythm of the day' rather than a structured timetable, and our caring, dedicated educators invite our youngest pupils to join a variety of activities designed to allow each child to reach the next step in their development.
We believe that children are confident, capable learners from birth and our Nursery School offers an enriched Early Learning curriculum which supports this approach. From stage 4, our core childcare staff are supported by experts in music, dance, drama, sport, visual arts, and modern foreign languages.
Our Early Learning facilities are carefully designed to meet the specific needs of each preschool age group and to offer a nurturing home-away-from-home environment that ensures every child feels comfortable and happy while learning and reaching their full potential.
Why Choose Our Nursery School in Wokingham, Berkshire?
At our private Nursery school in Berkshire, we believe in doing things differently. Our world-renowned early childhood education is based on our Early Learning philosophy that children are inherently curious, confident and capable learners, so we adapt our Nursery curriculum to follow their lead - closely observed and stimulated by our team of outstanding educators.
At our private Nursery School in Wokingham, we make full use of the school's magnificent parkland and forest, while our rooms provide limitless opportunities for exploration and discovery.
When the children arrive each day at our Nursery School, they are welcomed into each room personally by the educators who support them. We understand that for the children, this transition between home and school is between the two most important worlds in their life.
We nurture and support the children in our care so that they can make the best possible start to their Early Years education, while also preparing them for the transition to Junior School.
Nursery School Options
At our Nursery School, we offer a School Day or Extended Day option for our families.
School Day children arrive at 8.30am and are collected at 4.00pm. Their day includes a morning and afternoon snack, as well as a hot meal at lunchtime.
Our Extended Day children arrive at 8.00am and have the flexibility of being collected between 4.00pm and 6.00pm. Their day includes breakfast, lunch, and tea, as well as a morning and afternoon snack.
We also offer Add-ons, subject to availability, for breakfast between 8.00-8.30am and tea between 4.00-5.00pm.
For more information about our Nursery School options and prices, please visit our Fees page.
Nursery Early Education Programme
At our Early Learning School we encourage children to develop their innate curiosity, and help them to make sense of the world around them. Our Nursery School curriculum has a broad starting point so that we can use each child's unique interests and skills to shape their learning journey and our expert Nursery teachers are there to support, guide and encourage them every step of the way. Core skills are included in the Early Learning curriculum, including phonics and maths.
Our Early Learning programme also celebrates the concept of 'the hundred languages' of the child, which represents the many ways children express themselves. This approach broadens the Nursery curriculum and the lessons are integral to our daily programme with teachers incorporating them into class themes in Stages 1-3. In Stages 4 and beyond, our dedicated practitioners work with smaller groups to nurture skills and foster imagination, bringing a richness to our young students' work across a variety of subjects.
We follow the Reggio Emilia Inspired Learning approach and believe that children are born with the capacity to learn: we value them as confident and capable from birth. Your child is naturally curious and learns by asking questions and experimenting.
Children in this age group are also learning to express themselves in different ways, the ‘Hundred Languages’. Creative development through the visual and performing arts allows your child to develop his or her unique talents and imagination and we encourage this by providing lots of opportunity for open-ended play and emphasising the process as well as the end result.
This is an exciting time as children develop socially and emotionally. Our Stage 4 environment encourages the children to play together, offering large areas for creative activities, block play and small world role play. As their language development thrives, the children begin to create really rich and imaginative worlds in their play and enjoy inviting others to join in.
We begin to introduce our creative specialist teachers at this stage, who will help your child develop the different skills needed to add new depth to their ‘Hundred Languages’. Specialist teaching in Art, Dance, Drama, Sports and French are part of the core curriculum and we make sure there is a time for reflection at the end of each day so that the children can think about what they have discovered and the important connections they have made.
Reggio Emilia Inspired Approach
The Reggio Emilia Inspired Learning approach views our children as confident and capable learners from birth. We encourage children to develop their own theories and explore them with friends so they can make sense of the world. We listen to their ideas and take them seriously, supporting their natural curiosity by providing a wide range of experiences and nurturing positive interactions with well-trained, professional staff.
Your child is naturally inquisitive and our classrooms provide a million opportunities for exploration and discovery. Each room offers a flexible space that can be configured to provide opportunities for different types of play, with a lightbox area and space for creative development. In each area of the classroom, little pockets of interest are placed to invite children into play. These resources are deliberately chosen to spark curiosity, engage their interest and develop thinking.
Preschool Subjects
Our specialist lessons are a core part of our daily Early Learning School curriculum. In stages 1 to 3, these opportunities for creativity and self-expression are led by the Stage Teachers. In stage 4 and stage 5 (Reception), this work is guided and taught by our Practitioners, who work with smaller groups of children to hone skills and explore creativity and imagination. The specialist areas provided for this work include: art and discovery areas at each stage, our small performance hall, our light and dark area, and the fields and sports facilities. These lessons provide our children with the opportunity to work in exceptionally beautiful and purpose-built Early Learning School environments.
Our preschool children are introduced to art, drama, music, dance, French and P.E/sports. They have lessons in each of these areas weekly to develop skills, confidence and talents in expressive and performing arts, sports and languages. Productions and showcases are an important part of our work in the Nursery School, allowing children to highlight their growing talents.
A Stimulating, Purpose-Built Early Learning Environment
The layout of the physical space at Reddam House Nursery School has been designed to encourage choices, problem-solving and exploration. This environment plays a central role in the process of making learning meaningful.
Although it may not be possible to reflect the genuine buzz of excitement in our classrooms on the static page, our spaces are designed to spark creative curiosity and joy, as the children discover new things and form new relationships.
We encourage communication and collaboration through play and it is these elements that make our nursery such a welcoming and special place to learn.
The resources provided in our Nursery School are thoughtfully incorporated to encourage creativity, problem-solving, experimentation, exploration and open-ended play. Our environment offers real experiences with real items, often nature-inspired with natural light, big windows and mirrors.
Our Nursery children also explore the woods daily, from our youngest in buggies to our oldest, walking with their peers and teachers. We believe that infants need equal opportunities, indoors and outdoors, to explore their environment, from the coloured, bubble machine in our sensory room to the flora and fauna in our woods.
Nursery Facilities
Our Nursery School rooms are calm, beautiful and organised. Each space is carefully designed with natural objects and matched with palettes of paint or jars of crayons intended to inspire the children to explore colour, shape and pattern. Construction areas encourage children to deep dive into imaginative play and in each corner of every room they will find something to spark their interest and in doing so, direct their learning.
Alongside our warm and inviting classrooms, we have a soft play room, art and discovery area, library, and performance hall - all of which enrich the experiences of our youngest children and provide opportunities for physical development, singing and dancing.
Our Skilled and Passionate Nursery Teachers
Our preschool educators are skilled observers and childcare experts who determine individual needs and build on the existing skills and talents of the children in their care. We have an excellent balance of qualified early-years teachers and educators with a wealth of experience and a passion for infant education. They are all also first aid trained. Our Nursery teachers use an online journal to collect evidence and observations of learning and progress, sharing it with parents throughout the term.
Nurturing Relationships at Early Learning School
Parents are a child’s first teacher and collaboration with parents plays an essential part in supporting the holistic development of your child. The process of consultation and collaboration with parents allows us to support them in their role as the most important part of a child’s life. By providing a Nursery environment that feels safe, children will be able to feel confident enough to express their needs through a sense of belonging and well-being. Happy children grow in confidence and resilience, so strong relationships with staff and peers are very important to us.
Embracing Individuality
We focus on recognising and celebrating each child's innate abilities. Our Inspired approach centres around the child, who we believe is strong, competent, resourceful, and capable of constructing their own knowledge and understanding. How do they do this? Through exploration, self-expression, and working together with their teachers and peers.
We are guided by the children's interests and follow each child's individual line of enquiry, extending them in all areas of their development through their own individual interests. For example, if we have a child who consistently wants to play with cars in the construction area, we will use this to extend their learning in our role play, numeracy, literacy and mark-making areas.
From babies to school-age children, Reddam House Berkshire is an inspiring place to grow and learn. Discover how our private Nursery School in Wokingham can set the foundations for success in the following academic stages.

pageCache.text:
Senior School in Wokingham, Berkshire
Secondary Education at Reddam House Berkshire
Reddam House Senior School | Years 10 & 11
Our Secondary School in Wokingham, Berkshire unlocks the potential of students in Years 10 and 11 with a world-class GCSE curriculum that is both challenging and flexible. At Reddam House our rigorous academic, creative and sporting education is designed to challenge and engage our students, providing a secure foundation for progressing to the Sixth Form and beyond.
Our exceptional Secondary School programme is delivered by experienced and dedicated teachers who get to know each and every student, and are a vital part of their success in their GCSE exams at the end of Year 11. This high standard of teaching and learning is reflected in the consistently outstanding GCSE grades achieved by our Secondary School pupils, which far exceed the UK national average.
Why Choose Our Senior School in Wokingham, Berkshire?
Our Secondary School in Berkshire, UK provides a world-class Senior School curriculum that is both broad and dynamic. With a focus on exceptional academics, sports and the arts, our secondary education provides a complete foundation for GCSE and A-Level success and our commitment to nurturing academic excellence ensures that students secure exemplary results in GCSE exams every year.
Pupils are supported by our dedicated team of educators and are challenged with initiatives such as our CHEX (Challenge and Extension) Programme and Cycle Tests, exploring their chosen subjects with a depth of understanding that paves the way for outstanding academic and personal achievements.
Secondary School pupils also have access to the most extensive co-curricular and enrichment activities programme in the county, enabling them to extend their learning and broaden their horizons, fostering well-rounded development within a vibrant school community.
Secondary School Curriculum
Chosen in the spring term of Year 9, a broad range of GCSE subjects are available to our students. With an emphasis on personal enquiry and independent study, Reddam House Secondary School's curriculum appeals to the unique strengths and ambitions of each student.
Secondary School students generally study 10 subjects, which include Maths, English (Language and Literature), Physics, Chemistry, and Biology as standard, and then choose a further four subjects from a selection of options that include Computer Science, History, Geography, French, Spanish, Drama, Art and Design, Dance, Physical Education, Media Studies, Business Studies, and Music.
The regular Cycle Tests which are part of our programme mean that Secondary School students are regularly revising using past paper questions, online quizzes and flashcards among other things in preparation for the next Cycle Test.
Qualifications in Our Senior School
In our Secondary School in Wokingham, Berkshire, students sit GCSEs in Year 11, and choose between A levels and BTECs in the 6th form.
The Higher Project Qualification (HPQ) is a research qualification that is roughly equivalent to a GCSE. Students start this qualification in Year 9, finishing it in Year 10. It allows students to discover the joys of independent learning, take responsibility for their own study and develop new life and study skills. It has been designed to stretch and challenge students, by developing important academic skills required at higher education. These skills include referencing; essay writing; creating a bibliography; creating a presentation; and researching and deploying secondary and primary sources.
Secondary School Teachers
Our teacher selection policy for Secondary School is one of the most important aspects of Reddam House. We understand how crucial good teaching is, especially at Secondary School level, and pride ourselves on hand-picking outstanding members of staff with specialist knowledge, exemplary qualifications and a dedication to helping students reach their full potential. Our Secondary School teachers ensure pupils get the very best guidance and advice throughout their schooling, in order to achieve the best results in their GCSEs.
Co-curricular Activities in Secondary School
Preparing secondary students for life beyond school extends far beyond the classroom, which is why we are so fortunate to have an enthusiastic Outdoor Adventure Department that oversees our vast extra-curricular offering.
Our rich extra and co-curricular programme ensures we provide our pupils with numerous ways to stay active, while also challenging them to develop their skills and experience in a broader range of activities.
Teamwork is at the heart of many of our activities, helping instil a genuine camaraderie and togetherness in both winning and losing as a team. The experiences students gain here cement friendships, and see them develop the resilience and strength of character they need to succeed both academically and in life outside of school.
Co-curricular Activities & Clubs in Secondary School
Senior School students are expected to sign up for two after-school activities per week, with CCF on a Thursday being compulsory for Year 10. The aim of our programme is to add value to the student experience by allowing them the space and time to develop socially, academically and physically. Options available are extremely varied and can include the following:
All senior pupils are expected to progress through the various levels of the Duke of Edinburgh award and pupils in Years 9 and 10 participate in the Combined Cadet Force (CCF), which trains cadets in skills such as first aid, map reading and survival. Termly field days, together with weekend and summer camps give cadets the opportunity to enhance their skills at local military training bases, alongside professional members of the armed forces.

Sports at Secondary School
At Reddam House Berkshire, we are passionate about sport and outdoor pursuits. Our excellent facilities, including sports courts, fields and an indoor swimming pool, allows our senior students to take part in a variety of sporting activities, including: football, rugby, hockey, netball, tennis, gymnastics, swimming, athletics, circuits, fitness training and pilates. In addition, work on nutrition, lifestyle and exercise physiology takes place in the A2B (Aspire to Be) Programme.
Tuesday and Wednesday afternoon fixtures offer an opportunity to take part in competitive leagues and matches against local schools. We see the value in the collaborative element of team games and students are encouraged to participate in House sporting events too.
Arts at Secondary School
Senior students at Reddam House explore various expressive and performing arts subjects at GCSE level. Dance, Drama and Theatre Studies, Music, Art and Design offer a creative outlet for students and a rigorous academic curriculum with which to complement the EBacc subjects. The department aims to provide many opportunities for pupils to act, direct, design, devise and produce. The Arts thrive as academic subjects at Reddam House and are taught throughout the school.
Even for those who do not choose to do Art and Design in Secondary School, the Art department is a wonderful place for students to express themselves. Students are welcomed into clubs and courses which take place outside of the core school day and encouraged to explore their creative talents further.
At Reddam House Berkshire, Dance is offered to all students until Year 9 when they can opt for GCSE Dance. We aim to expand our students’ physical, technical and expressive abilities through a focus on performance, choreography and appreciation of different dance styles and genres. Alongside termly units of work, students follow the RSL Jazz Syllabus and can enter for exams annually.
Examination and recreational classes are available in the Royal Academy of Dance Ballet, International Dance Teachers Association Tap, and Freestyle and Street with qualified and registered dance teachers. There is also an auditioned dance company that runs outside of the core academic day bringing a vibrancy to this area of the school.
Additional Options at Our Secondary School
The relationship between student and tutor develops during these vital examination years, creating a strong coaching relationship built on mutual respect. Tutors will be the first port of call for guidance and support in all areas of the curriculum and in the wider life of the school. Every student has two one to one meetings with their tutor every half term.
A2B: Aspire to Be Programme (Reddam's PSHE)
Our Aspire to Be (A2B) programme in Secondary School will help senior students develop lifelong skills in developing and maintaining relationships, leadership skills, oratory and presentation competencies and preparation for financial independence.
Learn more about our Secondary School in Berkshire and how it can prepare your child for outstanding success in GCSE exams, Sixth Form and beyond.

Accessibility for Visitors
Accessibility for Visitors
At Reddam House Berkshire, we are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive environment for all visitors. We recognise that visitors may have differing access requirements, and we aim to make reasonable adjustments wherever possible to ensure a safe and positive experience when visiting our site.
Letting Us Know About Your Access Requirements
We encourage all visitors to inform us of any access requirements in advance of their visit. This allows our site management team to plan appropriately and ensure suitable arrangements are in place. When booking your visit, event, or appointment, you will be asked whether you have any specific access or support needs. This may include, but is not limited to:
• Physical or mobility access requirements
• Sensory, neurodiverse, or cognitive needs
• Medical requirements
• Hearing or visual impairments
• Temporary injuries or short-term access needs
This information is shared with the relevant site management staff in advance so that reasonable adjustments can be planned and implemented where possible.
Pre-Visit Information and Accessible Formats
Pre-visit information, guidance, and forms can be provided in accessible formats upon request. This may include:
• Digital formats suitable for screen readers
If you require information in an alternative format, please let us know in advance and we will do our best to accommodate your request.
Access Limitations and Site Considerations
Reddam House is a large and varied site, incorporating historic buildings and outdoor areas. While we continue to improve accessibility across the estate, some areas may have access limitations, including steps, uneven surfaces, or restricted routes. Any known or relevant access limitations will be clearly communicated in advance and available via:
• Event or visit information
• Direct communication with visitors where appropriate
Where full access is not possible, we will seek to identify reasonable alternatives to enable visitors to participate safely and meaningfully.
If you have any questions regarding accessibility or wish to discuss access requirements before attending Reddam House, please contact us in advance. Early communication enables us to plan effectively and support your visit appropriately.

Careers
At Reddam House Berkshire, values-driven education and a through-school journey inspire lifelong success. With a focus on academic achievement, personal growth, and sport and performing arts, you will be part of the Reddam difference, helping shape confident, well-rounded individuals. Our picturesque campus, with state-of-the-art facilities and boarding from Year 7, offers a world-class learning environment that inspires both staff and students. Our team values collaboration and professional growth, ensuring you thrive in a fulfilling, rewarding career.
Learn More about Reddam House Berkshire
Part of Inspired Education
At Inspired Education, we offer an exceptional opportunity to join the world’s leading premium school group and shape the future of education.
Purpose & Growth Journey Join a global community with an unwavering commitment tot empowers over 90,000 students across 26 countries. As the fastest-growing education group, your contributions will directly impact our journey of continuous global expansion and excellence.
Career Development We believe in nurturing talent and offering endless possibilities for career advancement. With Inspired, you will have access to opportunities across our 118 schools, enabling you to pursue your ambitions on a global scale. 31% of our educators take on exciting new roles overseas, and over 26% of our head appointments are made from within.
Global Community & Collaboration You will become part of a diverse, inclusive team of more than 12,000 professionals from over 109 nationalities. Together, we cultivate a culture of respect, dignity, and inclusion, where your talents and experiences are valued and celebrated.
Leaders in EdTech & Innovation We are transforming education through advanced technology and cutting-edge innovation. We invest more than any other school group in AI, EdTech, and immersive learning, enabling our educators to personalise learning paths and improve student outcomes.
State-of-the-Art Facilities Our campuses are designed to reflect our progressive approach to education. You will work in an environment that encourages exploration, creativity, and student engagement. With access to the latest tools and technologies, you will have the resources to inspire and motivate students, helping them to thrive in a rapidly evolving world.
A Culture of Innovation & Growth We foster a growth mindset that extends beyond our students to our entire community. Together, we are shaping a future where education is dynamic, inclusive, and always evolving.
Learn More about Inspired Careers

Guiding Students Toward a Bright and Ambitious Future
The Reddam House Berkshire Careers Programme is coherent and supports our students moving through their education and onto their next stage of life.
It fully equips them to manage their future progression through participating in career activities and career learning opportunities.
Our school’s careers programme ensures equality and diversity throughout. We are driven to deliver a programme that is comprehensive and transparent to students, teachers, the senior leadership team, governors, parents/guardians, alumni and career partners.
Our aim is to support students in their aspirational career choices which match their individualism and uniqueness.

A-Levels
Our A-Levels Programme in Berkshire, Wokingham
In Year 12, Reddam House students choose 3-4 specialist subjects from a wide range of Advanced Level (A-level) courses. These courses are designed to cultivate critical thinking and academic excellence.
Over the course of two intensive years, our exceptional teachers and tutors guide each student so that they are fully prepared for the challenge of their Year 13 A-level exams, enabling them to earn a globally recognised post-16 qualification.
Our students achieve consistently outstanding grades at A-level, well above the national average. 90% of our students are offered a place at their first choice university, including top tier universities in the UK and abroad such as Oxford and Russell Group institutions.
Our A-level education in Wokingham, Berkshire equips students with the skills and knowledge to successfully transition to university and excel in life after school.
Top Benefits of Taking A-Levels at Reddam House Berkshire
A-level students at Reddam House enjoy engaging lessons with highly experienced and dedicated teachers, who embrace the latest educational approaches and digital tools.
Our students enjoy world-class facilities set in a 125-acre parkland campus, with a dedicated Sixth Form Centre which was extended and developed in 2023, to provide areas for both independent study and leisure.
Reddam House's exceptional teaching is complemented by an enrichment programme, ensuring that our students have everything they need to achieve excellence in their exams and gain a place at their first-choice university in the UK or abroad. The majority of our students exceed the national average and are supported by our innovative assessment programme which uses regular formal tests to support learning.
In 2024, most of our Year 13 graduates successfully secured places in their preferred courses at top-tier universities. These include some of the UK's most prestigious institutions, such as Oxford, Durham, Exeter, and Manchester, as well as renowned universities in the USA and Japan.
Excellent A-Level Results & Access to World-Leading Universities
Excellent A-Level Results & Access to World-Leading Universities
Our students achieve outstanding grades at A-level and go on to gain places at their first-choice university.
With our unique co-curricular and enrichment programmes and access to cutting edge technology, we help our students develop strong leadership, teamwork, communication and interpersonal skills.
Supercurricular Approach
Supercurricular Approach
Our world-class academic resources enable students to extend their knowledge, nurture their intellectual curiosity and gain a competitive advantage for their university applications.
Why Choose Our School in Wokingham to Study A-Levels?
At Reddam House we offer a wide range of A-level courses, including those which are most commonly required by universities (the 'facilitating subjects') - so our students can access the broadest variety of degree courses.
Our outstanding A-level tutors and teachers are committed to ensuring every student's academic growth and success, and our small class sizes mean that they can provide individual attention in a way that larger establishments cannot.
Students enjoy close and supportive relationships with their teachers which is instrumental in improving learning outcomes, and achieving success in their A-level results.
We encourage all our A-level students to take advantage of our exclusive Sixth Form Centre, where they can work independently in comfortable surroundings, preparing them for life at university.
Reddam House A-level students are supported as they learn, lead and give back to the school community, becoming well-rounded individuals who can reach their full potential.
Exceptional A-Level Results
In 2025 Reddam House students have achieved excellent A-level results once again, with 21% grades at A*, 53% at A*-A, and 78% at A*-B. These outstanding results are significantly higher than the national average and better than most of the other schools in the region.
Reddam House has also received the ALPS Platinum Award, which recognises the top 10% of schools for value-added progress.
A-Level Curriculum
In Year 12, Reddam House students choose four specialist subjects to study at A-level.
Our A-level curriculum is delivered by a combination of engaging classroom lessons, student-led research and coursework. We encourage students to follow subject pathways that will enable them to follow their desired future career, or give them the widest choice of options.
A-level students can choose subjects from the following options: Art and Design, Biology, Business, Chemistry, Computer Science, Dance, Drama, Economics, English Literature, French, Further Mathematics, Geography, History, Mathematics, Music, Physical Education, Physics, Psychology, and Spanish.
These subjects provide a diverse array of educational opportunities for our students, allowing them to explore their interests and build a strong foundation for their future academic and career pursuits. Students may revert to three subjects during the Autumn term if they wish.
A-Levels Subjects
At Reddam House, our most popular A-level subjects include Mathematics and Further Mathematics, Economics, Psychology and the traditional Sciences. Other facilitating A-level subjects include English, History (Ancient or Modern), Geography, Computer Science, French and Spanish. We have also recently added Sociology to our offering.
Ctechs on offer for those who want to take a more vocational route include an Extended Certificate and Diploma in Business Studies.
We also offer Theatre Studies, Fine Art, Music, and Dance as A-level options.
Our A-level choices are reviewed every year in light of each cohort’s strengths and ambitions, with new A -level courses added when the demand arises.
Extended Project Qualification
We strongly encourage our A-level students at Reddam House to take the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ). Highly regarded by universities, the EPQ is an academic extension that sees students work independently to produce a piece of work on a subject of their choice. Not only is the EPQ an indicator of a student's readiness for university, but it also provides interesting collateral for university statements, CVs and job applications.
The EPQ is taken by some students in the United Kingdom and is equivalent to 50% of an A-Level, providing a Level 3 qualification. It is graded A*–E and worth up to 28 UCAS points.
A-Level Assessment & Grades
A-level grades range from A* to E and are often an entry requirement for universities. Certain university courses may require specific A-level subjects with a minimum grade prerequisite. Assessment requirements depend on the specific A-levels chosen.
A-level assessments provide external examiners and teachers with insights into how effective teaching and learning have been for each student. Formal assessments may also be helpful in understanding how well pupils are performing in a particular subject.
Most A-level subjects require students to sit one or more exam papers; however, this depends on the subject. All A-level assessments take place at our school in Berkshire, and pupils will receive their A-level results in August.
A-Level Requirements to Study
Advanced Levels are a UK subject-based qualification which provides an intensive and specialist education in a focused range of subjects. They are a Level 3 post-16 qualification that requires studying three or four subjects for two years, with exams at the end.
Students are encouraged to study 3 subjects but may choose to start the Sixth Form with 4 if they are undecided between two subjects and want to try both for a short period of time. Universities make offers based on 3 A-level subjects and therefore only those that can cope with a very high workload should consider studying 4 A-levels (students achieving straight 8/9 grades at GCSE). Those who choose 4 A-levels will be monitored to ensure that the extra A-level is not detrimental to their other subjects. If it is felt the student is not coping, they will be asked to drop their fourth option.
View our complete Sixth Form curriculum booklet for entry and assessment requirements for individual subjects.
Cycle Tests
To continually evaluate their progress during this 2-year programme and prepare them for their final A-level assessments, we give students an hour-long examination at the end of each week - a cycle test, based on their A-level subject choices. These tests are also a means of identifying and rewarding those pupils who work hard and achieve consistently good results.
Choose Reddam House Berkshire for excellent preparation in A-levels and access to top universities worldwide.

Thank you for considering our school for your child. We hope you will join us at one of our regular Open Day events; this is the best way to discover our unique school and get a sense of our strong culture, which celebrates the individuality and special strengths of every student.

Middle & Senior School

Students wishing to enter our Sixth Form are asked to attend an interview. Offers are conditional, depending on each student's final GCSE grades and subject to availability. When you are ready to progress your application, we will ask for a reference from your child's current school. Formal offers are made to successful candidates by the Principal. To accept, we ask that you sign our acceptance form and pay a deposit, which is refundable when your child leaves.
Discover how we can help your child fulfil their learning potential from 3 months to 18 years old.

FAQs
General Questions About Our School
When Should I Submit My Application?
We recommend applying at least one year prior to the desired date of entry to secure admission. Applications to join Reddam House Berkshire are accepted throughout the year and entry will be granted depending on assessment outcomes and availability. If you live outside of the UK, please contact us to make arrangements to organise a remote assessment.
For more information regarding student applications, please visit our Admissions Process page
Is There a Waiting List?
Yes, we usually have a waiting list for some age groups, which is why we recommend that parents apply well in advance. Please contact us for up-to-date information.
Is There a Sibling Policy?
Most siblings of current students join us at Reddam House Berkshire. Even though they have priority over other prospective pupils, admission is not automatic, and there may be occasions where the school judges that a sibling is likely to thrive better in a different academic environment. Please contact our admissions team to learn more about our sibling's policy.
Is There a Minimum Age for Boarding?
At Reddam House Berkshire we offer an exceptional boarding experience for students from 11 to 18 years old (Middle and Senior Schools from Year 7 upwards).
Are There Any Entrance Tests?
At Reddam House, our admissions process is designed to identify students who can benefit from our balanced and well-rounded education and who will make a positive contribution towards school life. Prospective student selection is based upon academic merit, which from Year 3 is assessed through an entry examination. Aligned with your child’s assessment results, we will then be seeking to identify those children to whom we can offer a good fit academically, socially and pastorally. Rest assured that the entire process is supported by our friendly admissions team, who will be happy to assist you with any questions or concerns.
What Are Your Class Sizes?
We have classes of up to 20 students. Our small class sizes allow for a greater degree of personal attention and student success.
What Is a Typical School Day Like? Do You Offer Wrap-Around Care?
Our school day begins at 8:30 am and ends at 4:00 pm. Pupils must arrive for registration by 8:30 am. Lessons start at 9:00 am and each lesson lasts for 55 minutes. Activities start in the second week of term and run on Monday to Friday during Term Times, from 4:15 pm to around 5:15 pm.
Our Early Learning School and Junior School offer extended days from 8:00 am-6:00 pm. Middle and Senior School students have extended day options with our boarding community, including early breakfast (7:30-8:00 am), supper (6:00-6:30 pm) and supper & study (6:00-8:30 pm).
Is There a School Uniform?
Yes, pupils from Stage 4 to Year 11 are proud to wear the Reddam House uniform as it creates a sense of belonging to our school community. Our Sixth Form students dress in a manner suited to the working environment. For more information about our uniform policy, please visit our School Uniforms page.
Is There a Forum for Parents to Get Involved?
Yes, the Reddam House Parents & Friends Association (PFA) gives parents the opportunity to get involved with our school. Their mission is to enrich the experience of all children at Reddam House, bringing together parents, teachers and children to raise funds and strengthen our sense of community.
Is There a Co-curricular Programme?
Yes, we offer an extensive enrichment programme spanning arts, sports and personal development, including activities such as Scuba Diving, Table Tennis, Basketball, Tennis, Golf, Animation, Movie Making, Art and Media, Bread Making, Chess, Cross Country Running, Dance, Debating, Fencing, Gun Club, Journalism and News, Medical Society, Mountain Biking, Music, Theatre and Drama. For more information about our extracurricular and co-curricular clubs and activities, please visit our co-curricular page here.
Is There a Super-Curricular Programme?
Yes, we have a super-curricular programme co-ordinated by a member of our academic staff. It includes visits and links to academic institutions. Opportunities are shared with students and parents.
Is There a Holiday Programme?
We run our own Summer Camps Programme during the summer holidays. Reddam House Summer Camps are open to students from all Inspired Education schools and other institutions worldwide and are filled with excitement, activities and challenges. Located in our stunning 125-acre private campus, children from around the world come together for a summer of unforgettable experiences including STEM, archery, bushcraft, dance and drama activities. Visit our Summer Camps page for more information.

Co-curricular Activities
Nurturing Skills & Talents Beyond the Classroom
Successful preparation for life after school comes as much from the student’s experience outside of the classroom as it does within. Reddam House Berkshire provides a vast range of clubs, co-curricular and extracurricular activities, spanning art, dance, drama, music, public speaking, societies, and sports. In addition to presenting students with the opportunity to explore new interests and build friendships, these activities encourage every child to find something to develop the personal qualities, attitudes and skills to complement their academic success, becoming well-rounded individuals, ready to tackle any future challenges.
The Best Clubs & Activities for a Holistic Development
Our school offers a diverse range of co-curricular activities, catering to a wide array of interests and passions. From sports like scuba diving, football, and tennis, to creative pursuits such as animation, movie-making, and art, we provide extensive opportunities for students to explore their interests, learn new skills, and thrive outside the classroom. With options like debating, fencing, journalism, and medical society, our co-curricular offerings foster personal growth and enrich the overall school experience.
Junior, Middle & Senior
Whether your passion is for the stage or you are happier in the Tech box, there are activities to suit all age groups and tastes. At various times of the year, rehearsals for major productions or competitions take centre stage. Debating is another popular pastime at all levels, with opportunities to take part in inter-house and external competitions. Public Speaking is taught as a timetabled lesson for all students until the end of Year 9 and is also offered as an extracurricular activity. This helps students foster strong research, oratory and listening skills that will be vital for their future success at university, their personal lives and careers.
Dance classes are open to everyone and include choreography, performance, ballet, tap, contemporary, street dance, Jazz, and ballroom.
From ‘Make and Do’ and sketching club in the Junior Wing to photography and screen printing in the Mansion House, Art is an important part of the extracurricular offering at Reddam House. Photography, screen printing, sculpture, textiles, watercolours, oils and much more allow students to enjoy some creative downtime in the magnificent art studios.
We also offer animation, movie-making, art and media.
With a fantastic range of facilities on offer, our Sports Department provide a rich and varied activities programme. Our younger Juniors have the opportunity to take part in skills development clubs honing their techniques to join the more sport-specific clubs for the older pupils.
Depending on the season, match practice may be supplemented with tennis, athletics, and cross-country running. Swimming clubs and teams practice early morning and afternoons with students benefitting from professional coaching advice. We also offer scuba diving, mountain biking and golf.
Sometimes, you just enjoy a subject so much, that you cannot get enough of it! Maths Clubs for all ages, Science Crest Awards and Creative Writing offer an opportunity to explore your passions outside of the curriculum while taking your skills to the next level.
In our Junior School, we offer verbal and non-verbal reasoning practice, great for developing flexibility of approach, vocabulary and patterning skills. Regular practice of timed papers helps hone examination skills too.
We also offer drop-in sessions for students who may want to review material with a member of staff or to gain further practice in a subject area.
Coding, robotics, website design and creating apps are all useful skills to have in today’s world. Utilising iPads and Surface Pro technology our students can start to build these skills developing proficiencies in these important and creative areas.
From Book groups, Bread Making, Brainiacs Challenges, Warhammer, Chess or board games, sometimes the only thing you want to do is relax and have fun. We have a range of clubs on offer which provide an escape from the busy day and time with friends.
Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme
Duke of Edinburgh Award Scheme
There is always great excitement in Year 9 as the students begin their first DofE Award, Bronze. Students undertake training in navigation and safety and then a practice hike before completing the assessed event. Many students opt to use one of the other extracurricular activities as their skill or physical component and we offer support to students wishing to undertake some aspect of volunteering through the school.
As our own assessing and awarding centre, the expectation is that the pupils will progress through the various levels of the Award, from Bronze, Silver through to Gold by the time participants leave the School. It is always a cause for great celebration when students visit the Palace to receive their Gold Awards!
Combined Cadet Force
Combined Cadet Force
Reddam House benefits from having its own Army section of the Combined Cadet Force (CCF). All Year 9 and 10 pupils have the opportunity to participate in the CCF, after which involvement is voluntary. The CCF helps to develop our students by introducing them to a plethora of activities and skills which assist in the steps toward adult life. Some of the activities include Leadership Training, First Aid, Map-Reading, Drill, Shooting, Field-Craft, Expedition Training and Survival Skills.
In Year 9, cadets work to achieve their Basic Proficiency Certificate and then progress to more advanced topics in Year 10. Senior cadets can then advance their personal training and expand upon their leadership skills by becoming Non-Commissioned Officers, with responsibilities including contribution to the training of younger cadets.
An integral part of the training is the termly Field Day where all cadets participate in a whole day of CCF activity. There are also several voluntary weekend exercises at local training areas, an annual adventurous training camp, during the October half term, and a military Summer Camp during the Summer holidays.
Senior cadets may also use their voluntary service towards completion of the Duke of Edinburgh Award scheme.
With 125 acres of grounds, Forest activities and exploration are always a popular offering in the school.
Gain Valuable Skills for a Lifetime of Success
An important element of our co-curricular provision at Reddam House is our House System. Students are allocated into different Houses, participating in various competitions held throughout the school year to accumulate points for their respective teams. This spirited competition fosters a strong sense of camaraderie and teamwork among our student body.
Teamwork is also at the heart of many of our clubs, helping instil a genuine fellowship and togetherness in both winning and losing as a team. The experiences students gain with these activities cement friendships and help them develop the resilience and strength of character they need to succeed academically and in life beyond school.
Music Lessons & Clubs
Music is an integral part of Reddam House. Every student is encouraged to learn a musical instrument and join our choirs, instrumental groups, and productions.
Our school boasts a dynamic music programme with peripatetic music teachers who make regular visits to instruct students in a range of instruments, including drums, piano, flute, violin, and singing. To further enrich the musical experience, we offer a variety of music clubs, including orchestra, ensemble, rock band, and choir, providing students with opportunities to collaborate and explore their musical talents in a supportive and creative environment.
The Reddam Adventure Department
The Reddam Adventure Department (RAD) is integrated into our well-being programme and encompasses much, from exciting, outdoor learning opportunities in Junior and Middle School to setting out on incredible adventures both in the UK and abroad. Our RAD is a unique element of the schools, providing opportunities for our students to learn and apply certain skills outdoors, experience adventure, and demonstrate resilience.
With our beautiful school estate as our 'classroom', students have the opportunity to develop courage, collaboration, responsibility, self-belief and challenge. Learning about our world through a variety of topics, from cooking to fire building, ecology to knots, children learn to succeed and fail as a team and defy their limitations.
Our students triumph in sports, excel in academics and inspire in the arts. Get in touch to find out how our exciting activities can enrich your child's educational journey at Reddam House.

Virtual Learning
Cutting-Edge Digital Tools to Enhance Learning Outcomes at Reddam House
Reddam House Berkshire is at the forefront of digital education to improve student outcomes and skills across age groups. Our school is committed to providing top-tier resources for academic success, and we have introduced the purpose-developed Global Study Platform, powered by Canvas, a renowned learning management system.
A Metaverse School to Unlock Your Child's Potential
Together with Inspired Education Group, Reddam House Berkshire is leading the way in immersive learning with its innovative Metaverse School which leverages virtual reality technology and turns lessons into dynamic and interactive experiences. Using this technology alongside traditional teaching methods and proven best practices in education boosts student understanding of key concepts and improves overall academic results.
Reddam House is the inspiration for creating the Metaverse school, a digital replica of the actual school building in virtual reality. Students at Inspired can access these virtual classrooms from anywhere in the world.
Providing Unparalleled Learning Opportunities with Virtual Reality
Providing Unparalleled Learning Opportunities with Virtual Reality
The groundbreaking VR initiative at Reddam House seeks to elevate students' understanding and memory retention by introducing novel and captivating ways to interact with the subject matter, hence facilitating and enhancing learning experiences for students. VR technology allows learners to explore different subjects in immersive ways, providing them with a competitive edge: Using VR headsets, they can manipulate objects physically, observe them from various angles, and gain real-time insights into their functions. This empowers them to undertake experiences which would not be possible in a traditional classroom setting, such as science experiments which would be too dangerous to perform, exploring the intricacies of the human heart or engaging with a mammoth up close. With VR, pupils can also study in otherwise inaccessible locations or environments.
Advance Your Child's Learning Experience in the Metaverse
Advance Your Child's Learning Experience in the Metaverse
VR enhances students' ability to retain information by immersing them in vivid, hands-on experiences across various subjects. By offering comprehensive perspectives from multiple angles and showcasing the functionality of objects, VR fosters a deeper understanding and ultimately improves learning outcomes.
In Geography, you can travel anywhere in the world instantaneously. In History, you can travel back in time to experience events first-hand. In English or the Arts, you can experience the inspirations behind famous works, gaining insights into the thoughts, feelings and experiences of the author. In Maths, complex concepts are made accessible and understandable through contextual activities and augmented thinking. In Science, you can make microscopic quantities massive and interact with challenging experiments surrounding radiation, anatomy, and out-of-this-world physics. Every subject can benefit from the power of VR learning, and every student’s learning can be enhanced through this exceptional technology. With bespoke lessons available across every subject area at Reddam House, designed by experienced teachers, students can enjoy the very best VR opportunities - all catered to their needs.
Outstanding Feedback from Our Community
Outstanding Feedback from Our Community
The metaverse has shown great potential for enhancing the quality of education at Inspired Schools. Inspired launched the metaverse pilot in 2022 and received extremely positive feedback from students, parents, and teachers, highlighting that VR and the metaverse make academic content more engaging, improving retention and understanding. With VR, students can explore landmarks and distant galaxies, conduct virtual experiments, and collaborate with peers from around the world from the comfort of their (physical) classrooms. The possibilities are truly limitless.
A New Global Study Platform to Enhance Learning Outcomes & Life Skills
At Reddam House Berkshire, we believe in providing the best tools and resources to ensure your child's academic success. After extensive discussions with students, parents and teachers on how to improve the learning experience, we have developed the Global Study Platform, powered by one of the best learning management systems in the world, Canvas (for more information on Canvas, please visit their website). The Global Study Platform is unique to Inspired and Reddam House Berkshire is the first to use it in the whole group!
The platform offers a range of benefits that will greatly enhance your child's learning experience:
Seamless Learning Environment
Through the Global Study Platform, your child will have access to an intuitive interface that brings together all aspects of their education - assignments, resources, grades, and more. This seamless digital environment allows for easy organisation and navigation, promoting a focused and efficient learning experience.
Improved Learning Focus
With all upcoming assignments and related course materials in one place, keeping ahead of busy schedules is easier than ever. In addition, the latest grades and ongoing grade progress visualisation provide students with a clear view of their learning performance.
Whether your child is at school, home, or on the go, they can access their course materials, assignments, and resources anytime, anywhere on their mobile. This flexibility fosters a personalised learning journey tailored to your child's needs and schedule.
Personalised Feedback
Canvas enables teachers to provide constructive feedback on assignments and assessments. This feedback loop encourages continuous improvement and empowers your child to excel in their studies.
As a parent, you will have access to view your child's course content and monitor their progress in real-time. This transparency allows you to actively participate in their educational journey and provide the necessary support.
